q: What should a carbon footprint claim on a product or website disclose so buyers trust it?
title: What a product footprint claim must state
short: State the number with its unit and what it covers: kg CO2e per declared unit, the life cycle stages included, the standard followed, the year of data, the GWP set, what was excluded and whether it was independently reviewed. A bare figure with no boundary cannot be compared or checked, so a careful buyer will discount it.

sections.h: The minimum to disclose next to the number
ul: Value and unit, for example kg CO2e per kg of product, per piece or per square metre.
Boundary: cradle to gate, cradle to grave, or gate to gate.
Standard: ISO 14067:2018 or the GHG Protocol Product Standard.
Reference period: which year's production and energy data.
GWP set and time horizon, for example IPCC AR6, 100 years.
Share of primary data from your own sites versus database values.
Review status: critical review, third-party verification, or self-declared.

sections.h: Items ISO 14067 says to report separately
ul: Offsets and carbon credits: not part of the footprint; show them separately if at all.
Biogenic carbon: report emissions and removals from plant-based materials separately.
Electricity: state how purchased power was treated, especially if you claim renewable supply.
"Low carbon" or "green" with no figure or comparison base.
"Carbon neutral product" when the claim rests on offsets; EU consumer law (Directive (EU) 2024/825) restricts this.
A comparison with a competitor's product that used a different boundary or standard.
A figure for one plant shown as if it covered all plants or all product grades.

p: On a product page or label, give the value, unit, boundary and standard in one line, and link to a short methodology note with the rest. ISO 14026 sets principles for this kind of footprint communication: the information must be relevant, transparent and not misleading, and the supporting report must be available on request.

example.title: Example of a disclosure line
lines: "2.4 kg CO2e per kg of grey cotton yarn, cradle to gate, ISO 14067:2018, FY 2025-26 data from our Coimbatore mill, GWP100 IPCC AR6."
"62% primary data. Excludes capital goods and packaging. Self-declared; not third-party verified."
example.note: Illustrative wording with a made-up value; use your own study's figures.

senseible: Senseible's product footprint calculator and records keep the factor and source behind every line, which supports a transparent methodology note. It does not review or verify a footprint claim, and it is not a substitute for an ISO 14067 study where a buyer asks for one.
